body_long:
La Petite Maison is no longer just a restaurant. Under chief executive Nicolas Budzynski, LPM Restaurants is adding new formats to the brand born in London in 2007.

## LPM-Sur-Mer, a first beach

On 28 November 2026, LPM-Sur-Mer opens at Jumeirah Beach Hotel in Dubai, in the space once occupied by Verde Beach. It is the brand's first dedicated beach concept, opening in stages: an indoor restaurant, a terrace, a laid-back lounge and the beach itself, with a salon bar where a DJ sets a livelier mood, and a private pétanque court. The menu keeps LPM's French-Mediterranean classics and adds dishes made for the waterfront. Music, wellness and family experiences are planned.

## Le Café LPM, from breakfast

A month earlier, on 23 October, Le Café LPM opened in Jumeirah. It is an all-day café, open from 7.30am, with the brand's first breakfast menu and an entirely new set of Riviera plates. In London, the café concept was announced for a year-long residency at The Lanesborough, from the Oetker Collection, from September 2026. Al Khobar, in Saudi Arabia, is listed as the next café.

## The restaurants keep coming

LPM opened at Four Seasons Hotel One Dalton Street in Boston in September, its first table in the north-east of the United States, with Gabriela Guitron as head chef. A restaurant at Rosewood Ranfaru, in the Maldives, is announced for 2027. For Budzynski, there is "more to come".

## The signal

The best restaurant brands now behave like lifestyle brands. Breakfast, beach and dinner under one name keep guests with the brand from morning to night, and give hotel partners a ready-made reason to visit.
summary: LPM-Sur-Mer, the brand's first beach concept, opens on 28 November at Jumeirah Beach Hotel in Dubai, a month after Le Café LPM, its first all-day café.
